script.base: Close high-total game, not a blowout. The book has CHI only a point favorite with both teams in the mid-20s (CHI 26.2, ATL 25.2), so neither side is scripted to clock-kill from the first snap and the 51.5 total means a lot of plays. Base flow: Caleb Williams plays through the hamstring tag and CHI, without Kyle Monangai, hands the lead-back carries to D'Andre Swift while still throwing to Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Colston Loveland. Atlanta stays balanced: Bijan Robinson keeps the 65-carry, 425-yard weeks 3-5 rushing load, Brian Robinson mixes in (31 carries, 128 yards in that span), and Drake London (27 targets, 408 yards, 282 air) works a CHI defense that has already allowed 4.50 yards per carry and 13.61 YPA in the middle. Whoever leads in the fourth runs, but the spread is too small to assume which side that is.
script.flip1: Williams sits or is a decoy. He is Questionable with a hamstring and the only saved rush lines are 65 and 42, so a scratch turns CHI into a backup-QB chase game. Swift never banks Monangai's vacated carries because CHI is in empty sets. Atlanta leads and kills clock with Bijan and Brian Robinson. Bijan's rush over survives this flip; Swift's does not; CHI pass overs stall.
script.flip2: CHI scores early and leads by 10-plus. Atlanta abandons the run, Bijan's rushing line dies, and London, Kyle Pitts and Jahan Dotson targets rise into the middle of a CHI defense that allows 13.61 YPA there. CHI clocks the lead with Swift, so Swift's rush over survives this flip and Bijan's does not.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and this lost because the game was played through the air. A 51.5 total, Henderson out, Gordon and Stevenson questionable, and a CHI middle that has allowed 13.61 YPA pulled both offenses into a pass-first script, so neither back got the carry count the read needs. Bijan regressed from 6.5 yards per carry, Brian Robinson took a day inside his recent 16-to-62 range, and Bijan finished 72 or 86 while London's 96-118 form cashed the number that had no price. Williams played, but Roschon Johnson won Monangai's carries and Atlanta's 4.06 yards-per-carry front, with Za'Darius Smith active, held Swift to another 45-58 yard day. The joint kill is a pass-heavy shootout. A CHI lead kills Bijan only. A Williams scratch kills Swift only. That counter is strong enough to keep Swift at a lean and to refuse a same-game parlay, not strong enough to drop Bijan, whose carry share and the two missing linebackers are still the best overlap on the card.
slip_story: One base-script story only: CHI -1 at ATL, total 51.5, both teams run because nobody is laying a blowout number. The anchor is Bijan Robinson rush yards over 95.5 against the depleted CHI front (Edwards, Elliott, Odeyingbo out, 4.50 YPC allowed). Swift rush yards over 64.5 is the Monangai sleeper and belongs on a separate card, because his good flip, CHI leading and clocking it, is Bijan's bad flip, and Bijan's good flip, Atlanta leading after a Williams limit, is Swift's bad flip. Do not add London, Odunze or Burden overs to either ticket; those need the pass-heavy flip that sinks the rush legs. No touchdown legs, one market per player, and no parlay of the two rush overs into a blowout-dependent ticket.
